title: scuttle configuration
description: ~/.config/scuttle/scuttle.toml. Every key is optional; a key left out keeps its default.

start-at-login.description: Register scuttle as a login item.

workspaces.description: Workspaces across all displays, numbered from 1, one native Space each. On macOS 27+, scuttle creates and removes Spaces to match. On macOS 26, add and remove desktops in Mission Control.

follow-space-order.description: Renumber workspaces when Spaces are reordered within a display in Mission Control. Windows stay put; workspace settings follow the new numbers. Display assignments still win across displays. False keeps each workspace's number and moves its windows back at the next arrangement.

workspace-to-display.description: By workspace number, the display it lives on: a pattern (main, secondary, or a case-insensitive part of the display's name as `scuttle list-displays` prints it) or a list of them, the first that matches a connected display winning. Other workspaces, and these when no pattern matches, live on the main display.

default-tiling.description: Whether scuttle tiles numbered workspaces by default.

workspace.description: Tiling overrides for numbered workspaces on every display (1-based).

display.description: This workspace's settings while it is on one display, keyed by pattern: main, secondary, or a case-insensitive part of the display's name. Omitted keys come from the workspace's own settings.

fullscreen-width.description: The share of the width a fullscreen window takes on this workspace. Lone windows use it unless lone-window-width is set.

lone-window-width.description: A lone window's centred share on this workspace, over display and top-level values. If unset everywhere, uses the resolved fullscreen-width.

follow-app-activation.description: When Cmd-Tab or a Dock click activates an app on another Space, switch there with the fast switch. A table also names apps not to follow.

exclude-apps.description: Bundle IDs whose activation is not followed, such as a menu bar app whose popover counts as a window.

block-native-fullscreen.description: Bring a window that enters macOS's native full screen straight back to its workspace and show it with scuttle's fullscreen instead, so every window stays on a scuttle workspace. If false, macOS full screen is left as it is: the window is on a Space of its own, outside every workspace.

float-windows-without-fullscreen.description: Float windows that can't go full screen, such as Finder's copy progress, About This Mac and Calculator. A `layout tiling` rule tiles one anyway.

fullscreen-width.description: The share of the width, inside the outer gaps, that a fullscreen window takes, centred. Lone windows use it unless lone-window-width is set. Display and workspace tables override it.

lone-window-width.description: A lone window's centred share of the width inside the outer gaps. Workspace tables override display tables, which override this value. If unset everywhere, uses the resolved fullscreen-width.

column-width.description: A new column's width as a share of the display.

preset-column-widths.description: The column widths switch-preset-column-width steps through, as shares of the display. niri's thirds by default.

display.description: Overrides for one display, keyed by pattern: main, secondary, or a case-insensitive part of the display's name as `scuttle list-displays` prints it.

fullscreen-width.description: The share of the width a fullscreen window takes on this display. Lone windows use it unless lone-window-width is set.

lone-window-width.description: A lone window's centred share on this display, over the top-level value. Workspace tables override it. If unset everywhere, uses the resolved fullscreen-width.

active-color.description: Colour of the focused window's border.

order.description: below draws the border directly below the window. above draws it above, as a ring that never covers the window's content or takes clicks.

rules.description: Independent per-window border rules. Last match wins; global disable and exclude-apps veto. Reload applies to existing windows without changing placement.

app-id.description: The app's bundle ID, e.g. com.apple.Safari.

app-id-regex.description: Case-insensitive regex found anywhere in the app's bundle ID, e.g. ^com\.apple\. for every Apple app.

app-name.description: Case-insensitive regex found anywhere in the app's name.

title.description: Case-insensitive regex found anywhere in the window title.

window-identifier.description: Case-insensitive regex found anywhere in AXIdentifier. An unavailable identifier never matches.

exclude-window-identifier.description: Reject this rule when AXIdentifier matches this case-insensitive regex. Unavailable identifiers are not excluded.

enabled.description: Whether matching document windows get a border, floating or tiled.

exclude-apps.description: Bundle IDs whose windows get no border.

focus-follows-mouse.description: Focus the window under the pointer once the pointer rests on it.

delay-ms.description: How long the pointer must rest on a window before it takes focus. 0 focuses as soon as the pointer stops.

swipe.description: Opt-in trackpad swipe focus between tiled windows. Native swipes can also switch Space or open Mission Control/App Exposé before the last window.

space-switch.description: Instant switches Space past the last window once the fingers lift. Native passes the whole swipe to macOS, so a full, quick swipe can both focus and switch Space. On macOS 27+, instant falls back to native.

vertical.description: Swipes up and down focus windows below and above. Always passes the whole swipe to macOS, which can also open Mission Control or App Exposé before the last window, regardless of space-switch.

animations.description: Windows glide to their tiles instead of jumping. Off while macOS's Reduce Motion is on.

duration-ms.description: Roughly how long a window takes to arrive. 0 jumps.

resize.description: instant sets a window's new size at once and glides only its position, which is smooth in every app. glide changes the size a step each frame too, smooth only in apps that redraw that fast.

drag.description: Dragging a tiled window with the mouse.

placeholders.description: While you drag a tiled window, outline the tile it came from and the tile it will swap with.

modifiers.description: mod, the modifier mod stands for in bindings, and which key of each modifier pair bindings answer to. The other key types as usual.

mod.description: The modifier mod stands for in bindings: alt, ctrl, cmd, shift, hyper or meh, or several joined by '-', such as 'ctrl-alt'.

alt.description: Which Option key is alt in bindings.

ctrl.description: Which Control key is ctrl in bindings.

cmd.description: Which Command key is cmd in bindings.

shift.description: Which Shift key is shift in bindings.

hooks.description: scuttle commands run on events. Shell goes through exec-and-forget.

startup.description: Once, when scuttle starts, after it has read the windows and displays.

workspace-changing.description: As soon as scuttle starts switching a display, and again when a burst of switches changes the target. exec-and-forget gets SCUTTLE_WORKSPACE (the target), SCUTTLE_PREV_WORKSPACE and SCUTTLE_DISPLAY.

workspace-changed.description: When a display's workspace changes or a switch settles or gives up, not on intermediate Spaces. With follow-space-order, also after renumbering even if the visible number is unchanged. exec-and-forget gets SCUTTLE_WORKSPACE, SCUTTLE_PREV_WORKSPACE and SCUTTLE_DISPLAY.

focus-changed.description: When the focused window changes, debounced by 50 ms.

display-changed.description: When a display connects or disconnects. exec-and-forget gets SCUTTLE_DISPLAYS and SCUTTLE_PREV_DISPLAYS, how many displays there are now and were before.

rules.description: Rules for new windows. Every rule whose conditions all match runs, in order; for layout floating and layout tiling the last one wins.

app-id.description: The app's bundle ID, e.g. com.apple.Safari.

app-id-regex.description: Case-insensitive regex found anywhere in the app's bundle ID, e.g. ^com\.apple\. for every Apple app.

app-name.description: Case-insensitive regex found anywhere in the app's name.

title.description: Case-insensitive regex found anywhere in the window title.

window-identifier.description: Case-insensitive regex found anywhere in AXIdentifier. An unavailable identifier never matches.

exclude-window-identifier.description: Reject this rule when AXIdentifier matches this case-insensitive regex. Unavailable identifiers are not excluded.

run.description: The command or commands to run for a matching window.

bindings.description: Key combinations mapped to the command or commands they run.

gaps.description: Gaps in points. A side or axis left out keeps its default.

inner.description: Points between tiled windows: one value for both axes, or per axis.

outer.description: Points between tiled windows and the screen edge: one value, or per side.

command.description: A scuttle command, as `scuttle help` lists them: `workspace 3`, `layout floating`, `exec-and-forget open -a Safari`. move-window-to-workspace, move-window-to-display and layout accept --window-id <id> to target a managed window on a numbered workspace.

commands.description: A command or a list of commands, run in order.

binding.description: A command or list of commands, optionally excluded for exact app bundle IDs.

command.description: The command or commands to run.

exclude-apps.description: Exact bundle IDs in which this key is passed through to the app.

fullscreen-width.description: The share of the width a fullscreen window takes on this workspace while it is on this display. Lone windows use it unless lone-window-width is set.

lone-window-width.description: A lone window's centred share while this workspace is on this display. Omitted values come from the workspace, then display and top-level settings, else the resolved fullscreen-width.

hook.description: A command or a list of commands, run in order. May be empty.

keyCombo.description: Zero or more modifiers (mod, alt, ctrl, cmd, shift, or the shorthands hyper and meh) and one key name, joined by '-': mod-shift-h, ctrl-left, alt-page-up, hyper-1, f5. mod is [modifiers] mod, alt by default.
